ELECTROCHEMICAL ENERGY CONVERSION

ADVANCED ELECTROCHEMICAL
MATERIALS FOR
SUSTAINABLE HYDROGEN

Welcome to the Energy Nano-material Process Laboratory (ENPL) led byProf. Soo-Kil Kim at Chung-Ang University. We design next-generation electrocatalysts, tailored 3D nanostructured electrodes, and interfacial architectures for high-efficiency water electrolysis and clean energy conversion.

CORE FOCUS

RESEARCH TOPICS

Our laboratory pioneers electrochemical energy conversion across three distinct research frontiers.

01

PEM WATER ELECTROLYSIS

Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis for High-Current Green Hydrogen Production
HEROERElectrocatalystsElectrode Engineering

Focusing on highly active and durable low-iridium/non-noble electrocatalysts and multi-scale structured catalyst layers for PEM water electrolysis. We develop advanced interfacial architectures that drastically decrease overpotentials during both oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER).

KEY INVESTIGATION AREAS
  • —Low-Ir and Ir-free nanostructured OER catalyst design
  • —Porous transport layer (PTL) / catalyst layer interface engineering
  • —Accelerated stress testing and degradation mechanism analysis
EXPLORE TOPIC DETAILS →
PEM WATER ELECTROLYSISPEMWE
02

AEM WATER ELECTROLYSIS

Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis Utilizing Cost-Effective Earth-Abundant Materials
HEROERElectrocatalystsElectrode Engineering

Developing noble-metal-free, high-performance transition metal electrocatalysts (Ni, Fe, Co-based alloys and oxides) and robust electrode frameworks operated in alkaline or pure-water fed anion exchange membrane environments.

KEY INVESTIGATION AREAS
  • —Non-precious transition metal multi-metal (NiFe, CoFe) catalyst synthesis
  • —Pure-water and dilute alkaline fed AEMWE cell architecture
  • —Anion-conducting ionomer/catalyst interfacial stabilization
EXPLORE TOPIC DETAILS →
AEM WATER ELECTROLYSISAEMWE
03

ELECTRODEPOSITION

Precision Electrochemical Nanofabrication of Advanced 3D Structured Electrodes
Nanostructured ElectrodesSelf-Supported ElectrodesAlloy / Multicomponent MaterialsElectrode Engineering

Pioneering tailored electrodeposition methodologies to fabricate self-supported, 3D porous, and multi-component nano-architectured electrodes directly on metallic substrates without polymeric binders.

KEY INVESTIGATION AREAS
  • —Direct electrodeposition of binary and ternary alloy nanostructures
  • —Dynamic hydrogen bubble template (DHBT) for hierarchical 3D foams
  • —Binder-free self-supported monolithic electrode fabrication
